A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PhysXNet datasets and PhysXGen framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material are readable and support comparison despite the title change and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset statistics, quantitative comparisons, component ablations, qualitative results, and error analyses, including the GPT-based comparison in Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental and dataset-analysis results, with revised physical-property evaluations in Tables 2, 3, and 5.

M1.justification: The dual-branch VAE and diffusion architecture, representations, losses, and module configurations remain unchanged. The added explanations of human refinement and corrected decoder labels in Figure 4 document the existing pipeline rather than establish a new method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation remain on PhysXNet, with the same object categories and physical-property tasks. The PhysXNet-XL procedural collection and its categories were already described in v1; no new benchmark or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 5 retain TRELLIS, TRELLIS+PhysPre, and the TRELLIS+PartField+GPT-4o pipeline in their corresponding comparisons. The four component-ablation configurations also remain unchanged. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 replaces the common rendered-property MAE evaluation with Euclidean distance for scale, PSNR for density and affordance maps, PSNR on description similarity maps, and instantiation-distance evaluation of kinematics, reported as COV/MMD. This substantially revises the central evaluation protocol. Dataset splits, training settings, and geometry metrics remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish retraining.

E4.justification: Table 3 revises the evidence for VAE/diffusion coupling through the new physical metrics, including COV/MMD articulation results, while retaining the same four configurations. The annotation comparison, qualitative architecture ablations, and error-distribution analyses remain; no new robustness question is investigated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Figure 11 retains the same prediction-error distributions rather than introducing statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 5 replace the physical-property results under revised metrics. For example, Table 2 changes PhysXGen material MAE 0.141 to PSNR 13.01 and kinematic error 0.479 to COV 0.33/MMD 0.08. Geometry scores remain unchanged, and GPT-4o retains its description advantage. These are revised evaluations, not comparable performance gains across versions.

T1.justification: The physical-property assumptions, latent definitions, and Equations 1–3 remain unchanged. The new evaluation metrics are named without introducing mathematical definitions, derivations, proofs, or formal guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: comprehensive physical annotations, the scalable annotation pipeline and procedural extension, and dual-branch generation that preserves geometry quality. The PhysX-3D title does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: The new ethics statement acknowledges representational bias and GPT-4o annotation biases that can persist despite human verification, and qualifies use in safety-critical applications. Existing explanations of normalization difficulties, spatial artifacts, kinematic limitations, and CLIP interpretability are retained.

D1.justification: v4 clarifies manual refinement of merged parts and human responsibility for kinematic annotation. It identifies the authors as annotators, discloses GPT-4o costs above $1,000, and adds ShapeNet licensing instructions. Conversely, the earlier ten-view physical-evaluation disclosure disappears. Architecture details, hardware, and the future-release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Collaborative Multi-Modal Coding, PhysX-Anything, and NAP, the last supporting the instantiation-distance metric. All earlier references remain, and the broader positioning against geometry-focused generation and partial physical annotations is unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order are retained. Changes include the PhysX-3D title, an author-name correction, localized annotation and evaluation rewrites, acknowledgments, and an ethics section. Existing appendices A–E become Sections 7–11 without substantive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 6 replaces three similarity-map panels with explicit dimensions, density visualizations, and kinematic outputs. Tables 2, 3, and 5 gain grouped headers and COV/MMD columns, while Figure 4 corrects encoder labels to decoder. Figures 3 and 8 and Table 4 move; most visual content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves transparency and interpretability through clearer human-annotation responsibilities, licensing and bias disclosures, corrected architecture labels, and explicit physical outputs in Figure 6. The evaluation overhaul remains incompletely documented: the ten-view detail disappears, and Section 10.1 retains a 24% scale-error reduction although revised Table 5 gives 8.81 versus 7.24, approximately 18%. These reporting shortcomings limit the overall gain.
